summary: Xianlin Ji (1911–2009) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Tsinghua and under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg at Göttingen (PhD). He served as professor, vice president, and Life Professor at Peking University, and held leadership posts at CASS and CAS.

Xiaoling Wu (1914–1995) worked in Sinology and Indology. He held posts as a research scholar and lecturer at Visva-Bharati University (~1942–1946), at Peking University (~1947–1949), and as professor at Academia Sinica (~1950–1977) and CASS (~1977–1995).
Xiaoming Hou is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Hou was a doctoral student at Ghent University (attested 2026) and served there as a postdoctoral researcher (attested 2026).
Xiaoting Wei is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies who completed an MA at the National University of Singapore under supervisor Cheng-Mei Ku (attested 2004).

Xinchuan Huang (1928–2021) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. After studying at Peking University (~1956–1958), he served at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–2010), including as a researcher at its Institute of Asia-Pacific Studies (~1988–1993).

Xinru Liu is a historian specializing in Indology and Central Asian history. She completed her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher (~1980–1985) and held posts at CASS (1993) and The College of New Jersey (~1993–2018).
Xiuzhi Zeng is a researcher in Buddhist and religious studies who earned an MA at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen (attested 2006).

Xu Dishan (1893–1941) was a scholar in Sinology and religious studies who studied at Yenching University, Columbia University, and Oxford. He held academic posts at Peking University (~1926–1935), Tsinghua University (~1930–1935), and the University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).

Xue Yu is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Yu served as assistant professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010), visiting professor at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), and professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist and religious studies. Zhang earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008) and served as an associate professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, having studied under Shoryu Katsura. Li held appointments as a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University (2011) and as Research Associate and researcher at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2026).
Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye and served as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Yadi Qu works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies, and is attested in 2026 as a student and Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg.

Yael Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington under Gregory Schopen, and became a professor at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 2000, 2026).

Yakupitiyage Karunadasa (1934–2026) studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of London under David Friedman (PhD). A specialist in Buddhist studies and philosophy, he was Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and taught at Kelaniya and HKU.
Yan Fu (1854–1921) was a scholar in philosophy and Sinology who studied at the Royal Naval College (~1877–1879). He later held posts at Fudan University (~1905–1906) and Peking University (~1912).
Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and Sinology, and earned a PhD from the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo.

Yang Wenhui (1837–1911) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), Zhiheng Jingshe (1908), and Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and served as head of the Buddhist Research Society, which he founded in 1910.
Yang-Gyu An is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Hojin and earned a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1998 under Richard Gombrich.
Yangdon Dhondup is a Tibetologist who earned a PhD from SOAS University of London (~2000–2004) under the supervision of Henry Y. H. Zhao.
